patient.chief_complaint: Progressive gait deterioration, memory decline, and new urinary incontinence — oncology team concerned about cancer recurrence or leptomeningeal disease
patient.history_present_illness: A 69-year-old retired nurse with breast cancer in clinical remission (6 years post-treatment) was admitted for urgent neurological evaluation of progressive gait deterioration, memory decline, and urinary incontinence over the past 10 months. She was treated with lumpectomy, radiation, and chemotherapy (doxorubicin-cyclophosphamide followed by paclitaxel) 6 years ago and has been in clinical remission on tamoxifen maintenance. Her oncologist and oncology team are alarmed because her symptoms — gait deterioration, cognitive decline, and urinary incontinence — could represent leptomeningeal carcinomatosis (LMC) recurrence, and they have requested urgent neurology consultation. She describes progressive shuffling gait beginning 10 months ago, three falls (no injury), and increasing reliance on a walker. Urinary urgency began approximately 7 months ago, progressing to frank incontinence 2-3 times per week. She describes increasing forgetfulness and difficulty following complex nursing reports she used to review voluntarily. Her oncologist noticed the gait change at a routine visit and was concerned about CNS metastasis or LMC. However, a neurology fellow who examined her noted the gait had a distinctly magnetic quality more consistent with NPH. A head MRI showed Evans index 0.35 and raised both LMC (leptomeningeal enhancement? — no enhancement present) and NPH as concerns. The critical diagnostic distinction is NPH (benign, treatable) vs leptomeningeal carcinomatosis recurrence (malignant, poor prognosis). CSF cytology and opening pressure are critical.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, oriented x3. Anxious about cancer recurrence. MoCA 22/30. Mild delayed recall (2/5), executive dysfunction. Normal language. No aphasia.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Normal. No papilledema. No diplopia. No facial numbness. PERRL.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal tone and strength. No focal deficits. No radiculopathic signs.
neurological_exam.sensory: Normal throughout. No dermatomal sensory loss.
neurological_exam.gait: Wide-based, shuffling magnetic gait. Freezing on initiation. TUG 27 seconds. 10-meter walk 21 seconds. Cannot tandem walk. Pull test — 2 steps backward.
neurological_exam.additional: No meningismus. No papilledema. No cranial nerve palsies (would suggest LMC). Bilateral grasp reflexes present (frontal). No skin lesions suggesting metastases.

signal_characteristics.description: No leptomeningeal enhancement on post-contrast T1

mri.impression: NPH imaging findings: Evans index 0.35, callosal angle 81°, partial DESH. Critically: NO leptomeningeal enhancement, no parenchymal metastases on post-contrast T1. MRI does not support leptomeningeal carcinomatosis recurrence. Findings support NPH as the primary diagnosis. CSF cytology at time of tap trial is essential to definitively exclude LMC. Clinical correlation recommended.

special_tests.flow_cytometry: No abnormal lymphoid or epithelial cell population — negative for malignancy

CEA_csf: 0.8 ng/mL (normal <2.0 ng/mL — supports no LMC).

specialized_test.test_type: High-volume tap trial (40 mL) — after negative CSF cytology confirmed

findings.urinary: No incontinence in 24h post-tap; decreased urgency

specialized_test.impression: Clearly positive tap trial: 30% TUG improvement, 33% walk improvement, 3-point MoCA improvement. Negative cytology confirmed before tap. NPH diagnosis confirmed — leptomeningeal carcinomatosis excluded. VP shunt is urgently indicated. Excellent prognosis given negative LMC and positive tap trial.

output.impression: Negative amyloid PET. No Alzheimer's copathology. NPH is the primary, sole neurological diagnosis. Excellent prognosis for VP shunt.
Mildly hyperdynamic aqueductal flow (20 cm/s, 70 mcL/cycle). Consistent with NPH pathophysiology.

findings.result: No evidence of breast cancer recurrence. No new mediastinal, pleural, or hepatic lesions. Prior lumpectomy site stable. No skeletal metastases on bone windows.

output.impression: No evidence of breast cancer recurrence on CT staging. Combined with negative CSF cytology and negative brain MRI for metastases, systemic and CNS cancer recurrence is excluded. Neurological symptoms are from NPH, not oncological recurrence.

results.title: NPH in cancer survivors — LMC mimicry and diagnostic algorithm
results.key_finding: NPH and LMC can have overlapping features (cognitive decline, incontinence); negative CSF cytology x2 combined with negative post-contrast MRI and positive tap trial effectively excludes LMC

results.title: False-negative CSF cytology in LMC — implications for practice
results.key_finding: Single CSF cytology sensitivity for LMC is 45-60%; three separate cytospin preparations increase sensitivity to >85%; negative x3 with negative MRI strongly excludes LMC

output.summary: Negative CSF cytology x3 (three cytospin preparations), negative post-contrast MRI, negative flow cytometry, and normal CSF CEA effectively exclude leptomeningeal carcinomatosis. The positive tap trial (30%) confirms NPH as the primary diagnosis. VP shunt is appropriate and cancer recurrence has been excluded through rigorous workup.

findings.finding: Neurogenic detrusor overactivity — involuntary contractions at 138 mL. No outlet obstruction or stress incontinence.

output.impression: NDO consistent with NPH frontal dysfunction. Not a paraneoplastic bladder process. Expected to improve post-shunting.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) — leptomeningeal carcinomatosis excluded

optimal_actions.expected_finding: LMC excluded — shunt appropriate; continue tamoxifen

critical_actions: Cytology x3 and flow cytometry BEFORE tap trial — cannot perform tap trial if LMC not excluded (malignant cells in CSF would change management entirely)
Post-contrast MRI brain before LP in any cancer patient with new neurological symptoms
Staging CT to exclude systemic recurrence
Continue tamoxifen perioperatively — do not hold
Document negative LMC clearly in medical record before proceeding to VP shunt
contraindicated_actions: Performing tap trial before cytology results in a cancer patient — could remove malignant CSF before cytology is adequately evaluated
Diagnosing NPH without ruling out LMC in a breast cancer survivor
Holding tamoxifen for surgical procedure — risk of cancer recurrence
key_reasoning_points: In any cancer patient with neurological decline, LMC must be definitively excluded before NPH workup proceeds
Three cytospin preparations of CSF cytology increases sensitivity for LMC from 45-60% to >85%
NPH imaging (Evans 0.35, callosal angle 81°, DESH) and positive tap (30%) confirm NPH after LMC exclusion
Negative post-contrast MRI combined with negative cytology and negative staging CT comprehensively excludes cancer recurrence
Tamoxifen must be continued perioperatively — not a reason to defer shunt surgery

red_herrings.data_point: Breast cancer history (in clinical remission 6 years) with new gait, cognitive, and urinary symptoms
red_herrings.intended_effect: All symptoms attributed to leptomeningeal carcinomatosis recurrence; NPH diagnosis missed or deferred pending cancer workup
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Comprehensive LMC exclusion (cytology x3, flow cytometry, CSF CEA, post-contrast MRI, staging CT) is all negative. NPH is the primary diagnosis confirmed by positive tap trial.

red_herrings.data_point: CA 15-3 at upper normal limit (28 U/mL)
red_herrings.intended_effect: Borderline CA 15-3 interpreted as evidence of cancer recurrence, delaying NPH evaluation
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: CA 15-3 is at upper normal limit and stable compared to prior surveillance (per oncology). Not a marker of recurrence in this context. NPH evaluation should proceed.
